method: 100 interactive sessions with stops, sampled (random.seed(679)) 20 per tool-call band 0-15/15-40/40-80/80-160/160+ from ~/.claude/projects on 2026-10-15; 4 sonnet subagents labelled each from a timeline of the user's words, tool calls, errors and replies, no counts shown, by the guide.
guide:
# Labelling guide: short simple session, or mid-length and longer?

The owner's words: "짧은 단순 수정 세션은 넘어가고 중반 이상 되는 세션은 포함하도록" — skip short, simple fix sessions; include sessions of mid length and longer. A hook will ask the agent to run a retro (a lesson review) at least once in each included session.

Each digest is one Claude Code session's timeline, split at its stops (turns the agent ended): the user's words (USER), the agent's tool calls, failed calls (ERROR) and what it said (SAYS); long stops are cut in the middle.

Label a session:

- `short`: a short, simple session: a quick question answered, a one-off small fix or tweak, a status check, a single short command run, a session that ended almost at once, or a few steps done with no struggle and nothing worth reviewing.
- `mid`: mid-length or longer: multi-step work, several files or rounds, a debugging hunt, a design or planning discussion, a session that coordinates other sessions or waits on reviews over many turns, or any session long enough that a retro could find a lesson.

Read every digest's timeline; judge the amount and kind of work done, not its length on the page: a session that mostly waits on monitors or sends status pings with little work is still short. When a digest is too cut to tell, open the transcript (JSONL) at its path and skim it.

Write one JSON object per session, one per line, to your output file, in digest order, the path copied from the digest header:

`{"transcript": "<path>", "label": "short"|"mid", "why": "<at most 12 words>"}`

Label every digest; a count mismatch is a failure to report.
